definition: The highest and final stage of capitalism characterized by the dominance of monopolies, the merging of bank and industrial capital into finance capital, the export of capital (rather than goods), the formation of international monopolist associations dividing the world, and the territorial division of the globe among the great powers — imperialism necessarily generates inter-imperialist war as monopoly capital competes for markets and resources
connective_patterns: imperialism as the highest stage of capitalism
imperialism generates inter-imperialist war
imperialism as the dominance of finance capital

definition: A disciplined, close-knit organization of professional revolutionaries drawn from the most politically conscious elements of the working class and intelligentsia, tasked with bringing socialist consciousness to the proletariat and leading the revolutionary struggle — the vanguard is necessary because the working class, left to its own devices, develops only trade-union consciousness rather than revolutionary class consciousness
connective_patterns: the vanguard party brings consciousness from without
the vanguard as the most advanced detachment of the class
the vanguard party and the masses in dialectical relationship

definition: The organizational principle combining democratic decision-making (open debate, election of leaders, minority rights during discussion) with strict centralized discipline (mandatory obedience to decisions once democratically reached); designed to ensure both internal vitality and external effectiveness in the revolutionary party's struggle against the bourgeois state
connective_patterns: freedom of discussion, unity of action
democratic centralism reconciles democracy and leadership
debate before the decision, discipline after

term: dictatorship of the proletariat/无产阶级专政
definition: The transitional state form between capitalism and communism in which the working class exercises political power over the defeated bourgeoisie — not a specific governmental form but the class content of the post-revolutionary state; Lenin emphasized that this dictatorship is democratic for the exploited majority while repressive toward the former exploiters, and must actively work toward its own dissolution through the withering away of the state
connective_patterns: the dictatorship of the proletariat as the transition to communism
democracy for the majority, dictatorship over the exploiters
the state that works toward its own withering away

definition: Lenin's 1917 theoretical work establishing that the state is inherently a tool of class oppression — whether democratic or dictatorial, the state serves the ruling class; the revolutionary task is not to capture the existing state apparatus but to smash it and replace it with a communal state (on the Paris Commune model) that progressively withers away as class distinctions dissolve
synonyms: the Marxist theory of the state
the withering away of the state
connective_patterns: the state as an instrument of class oppression
smash the bourgeois state rather than capture it
the withering away of the state through the dictatorship of the proletariat

definition: Councils of workers', soldiers', and peasants' deputies that constituted embryonic organs of democratic self-governance — the soviets surpassed bourgeois parliaments in democracy by excluding the propertied classes and organizing power from the bottom up; Lenin's slogan 'All Power to the Soviets' expressed the demand that these organs of direct democracy become the sole legitimate form of political authority
connective_patterns: All Power to the Soviets
soviets as embryonic workers' state
soviets surpassing parliament in democracy

term: what is to be done/怎么办
definition: Lenin's foundational 1902 pamphlet (Chto delat?) that establishes the theoretical case for a vanguard party of professional revolutionaries, arguing that the working class cannot spontaneously develop revolutionary consciousness and requires the organized intervention of revolutionary social democrats to transform trade-union consciousness into political class consciousness
connective_patterns: What Is to Be Done as the founding text of Bolshevism
the argument against economism and spontaneism
the organizational question as the key to revolution

definition: The structural form of the revolutionary vanguard built on democratic centralism — a network of professional revolutionaries organized in cells, with elected leadership, internal discipline, and the capacity for both legal and illegal work; party organization is not merely a practical arrangement but the material embodiment of revolutionary theory and the indispensable instrument for transforming spontaneous struggle into conscious revolutionary action
connective_patterns: party organization as the embodiment of revolutionary theory
from circle mentality to disciplined party organization
organization as the weapon of the weak against the strong

definition: Revolutionary socialist consciousness — the theoretical understanding of the totality of capitalist social relations, the historical role of the proletariat, and the necessity of revolution; consciousness must be brought to the working class from without by the revolutionary intelligentsia and the party, because the division of labor in capitalist society prevents workers from independently developing comprehensive political understanding beyond their immediate economic interests
connective_patterns: consciousness brought from without to the working class
consciousness vs. spontaneity as Lenin's central dialectic
consciousness requires theoretical work beyond immediate experience

definition: The working class's instinctive, untheorized response to exploitation — strikes, riots, machine-breaking — that represents 'consciousness in embryonic form' but cannot by itself develop into revolutionary political consciousness; spontaneity produces only trade-union consciousness (the struggle for better conditions within capitalism) and, if unchallenged by organized revolutionary leadership, leads to reformism and accommodation with the existing order
connective_patterns: spontaneity as consciousness in embryonic form
spontaneity leads only to trade-union consciousness
the dialectic of spontaneity and consciousness

definition: The fusion of bank capital and industrial capital under the dominance of banking monopolies — finance capital is the characteristic form of capital in the imperialist stage, where a financial oligarchy controls the economy through ownership of shares, directorships, and credit allocation rather than through direct production; it is the basis for the export of capital and the partition of the world among monopolist associations
connective_patterns: finance capital as the fusion of bank and industrial capital
finance capital dominates the imperialist stage
finance capital as the basis for capital export

definition: The stage of capitalism in which free competition has been replaced by the domination of monopolies — cartels, syndicates, and trusts that control entire branches of production; monopoly capitalism is not an aberration but the natural development of capitalism's competitive logic, where concentration and centralization of capital inevitably produce monopoly, which in turn generates imperialism
connective_patterns: monopoly as the natural product of free competition
monopoly capitalism as the economic basis of imperialism
concentration of production leads to monopoly

definition: The right of oppressed nations to secede and form independent states — Lenin supported this right as a democratic demand against imperialist oppression while insisting it be subordinated to the interests of the proletarian class struggle; national self-determination is a weapon against imperialism and great-power chauvinism, not an end in itself, and the proletariat of oppressor nations has a special duty to support it
connective_patterns: the right of oppressed nations to secede
national self-determination as anti-imperialist demand
the proletariat of oppressor nations must support self-determination

definition: The law that capitalism develops at different rates in different countries and sectors — uneven development means that the chain of imperialism breaks at its weakest link rather than at its strongest; this explains why socialist revolution occurred first in relatively backward Russia rather than in advanced capitalist countries, and why revolutionary situations arise from the contradictions between the most and least developed parts of the imperialist system
connective_patterns: the chain breaks at its weakest link
uneven development explains revolution in backward countries
the law of uneven development under imperialism

definition: The philosophical foundation of Marxism-Leninism combining Hegel's dialectical method with Feuerbach's materialism — matter is primary, consciousness secondary, and both nature and society develop through the dialectical laws of the unity and struggle of opposites, the transformation of quantity into quality, and the negation of the negation; Lenin defended and developed this against both idealism and mechanical materialism
connective_patterns: matter is primary, consciousness secondary
the three laws of dialectics
dialectical materialism as the philosophical basis of Marxism-Leninism
